rationale: The recovery experiment executed in a clean copy (2cd3883705a64c35aa04ba14b815ea42, completed, exit 0) with all three of its comparisons complete and satisfied: after being stopped, missed a committed payload, and restarted from its persisted storage, the member reported leader 1, fetched and applied the missed entry, and proposed successfully with the new payload committed. This update interprets that receipt, records the recovery observation as durable knowledge with its indices, and states the limits of the scenario.

knowledge.statement: A member restarted from persisted state in the retained three-node scenario recovered the committed entry it had missed and returned to full participation. Before the restart the node's committed and applied index were both 2; after the restart it reported leader 1, applied the entry committed while it was down (committed and applied index 3), the payload appeared in its applied entries and on all three nodes (observed_nodes [3,1,2]), and a subsequent proposal from it returned with no error and its payload was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, no message loss and no snapshots; node 2 stopped while a payload was committed by nodes 1 and 3, then rebuilt on the same MemoryStorage that the driver had updated with HardState and appended entries; ten rounds of ticks with delivery between rounds after the restart so the leader issued heartbeats; membership unchanged.

interpretations.rationale: The recovery obligation was satisfied in this scenario and the receipt is complete for it. Admission: the harness records the restart with the member's committed and applied index before the restart (index 36: node 2, commit_before 2, applied_before 2, payload_down named) after having stopped node 2 and committed that payload with the remaining nodes. Results: the restarted member reported leader 1 and recovered the missed payload (index 37: recovered true, commit_after 3, applied_after 3, observed_nodes [3,1,2]); a proposal from the restarted member returned with no error (index 38: returned true, err empty, leader 1), so its proposal gate was armed again after it observed the leader; and that proposal's payload was committed on all three nodes (index 39), so the member was not merely reading state but participating in decisions again. This is consistent with the source: a rebuilt instance loads Term, Vote and Commit from storage, learns the leader from heartbeats once the clock advances, catches up through the ordinary append path, and arms its gate when the run loop observes the leader change from none to 1. No defect is claimed. Note the contrast with the parent investigation's held-proposal effect: there the member is re-admitted while it already believes a leader is known, so no leader change is observed and the gate stays disarmed, whereas a restarted member starts without a leader and arms the gate when it learns one.
counterevidence: The clock was advanced by the harness after the restart; without ticks the restarted member receives no leader traffic in this setup, so the observation depends on the harness supplying clock progress rather than on the target alone.

The scenario keeps membership unchanged and takes no snapshot, so the storage's ConfState stays valid and catch-up uses the append path only; snapshot installation and storage loss are different recovery paths.
limitations: Single restart, single stopped member, reliable delivery, no ticks during the outage, no simultaneous restarts and no crash-stop during the restart.
No snapshot installation and no storage loss: the restarted member's storage contained all entries it had previously persisted, so only the entries committed while it was down had to be fetched.
One scenario instance; no claim about recovery under loss, partition or repeated restarts.
The three comparisons are complete holds for this scenario, which establishes the observed behaviour rather than a general guarantee.

knowledge.assertion: the restarted member recovered the missed committed entry and proposed successfully afterwards
the proposal gate is armed by an observed leader change, which a restarted member experiences when it first learns the leader
